threads.thread_goal: Align on subscription value proposition, tiers and pricing approach.

messages.text: Kicking off the new subscription-based product line work. For this first thread, we need to align on who we are targeting, the core value proposition, and the initial tiers and pricing approach so we can move on T1 and T2. @all, can the product managers share a first pass for target segments and a strawman of tiers so we can capture it in the Subscription Product Brief and Value Proposition doc and later reflect it in KPI Definitions and Dashboard Spec? I would like us to converge on a short list of segments and 2–3 tiers we will model in detail.

Thanks for starting this. Drafting a quick outline for T1: I suggest we focus on three primary segments: 1) existing customers with high engagement but low repeat purchases, 2) new digital-first customers acquired in the last 6 months, and 3) lapsed customers who bought once in the last 18–24 months. For the value proposition in A1, I am thinking along the lines of predictable savings, priority access, and simplified experience. For tiers, maybe: Basic (entry price, core benefits), Plus (most popular, better discount and perks), and Premium (highest benefits, limited audience). Before I write this up in A1, can others react to whether these segments and tiers feel directionally right?

This segmentation makes sense to me, especially the focus on existing high-engagement customers. From a revenue and margin angle, we should check that each tier can sustain a healthy contribution. For T2, I can start a simple pricing grid with list price, discount range, and expected ARPU per tier, then we can refine with finance. One question: do we want the Basic tier to be almost a no-brainer entry point, or should we push more value into Plus and make that the default choice?

I like the three segments and the three-tier structure. From a customer experience angle, we should make sure each tier has a clear story: Basic for trying the subscription with minimal risk, Plus as the best balance of savings and perks, and Premium for heavy users. For A1, I can draft a short value proposition statement for each segment and tier combination so we can test messaging later. On pricing, I would lean toward making Plus the anchor and framing Basic as a lighter option rather than the main one.

Good points. My instinct is to position Plus as the default choice, with Basic as a low-friction entry and Premium as an upsell for a smaller group. That should help with revenue while still giving an accessible option. Before we lock that in, can we quickly sanity-check the three segments against our current customer mix and expected volume? If someone can pull a rough count for each segment, we can see if any of them is too small to justify a dedicated focus.

I can take a first pass at sizing the three segments using our latest CRM export. I will not change any system setup, just use existing reports. I will estimate how many customers fall into each of the three buckets you listed and share a quick summary so we can see if the lapsed group is large enough to target in the first wave.

I can help by drafting the segment definitions in A1 so they are clear and consistent with how we will pull them from CRM. I will describe each segment with time window, spend level, and engagement markers. That should also make it easier later when we map KPIs in A6 and T6. Once we agree on the wording, we can reuse it in marketing briefs.

While @514149 pulls the counts, I will start a basic pricing model for T2 in a sheet aligned with A6. I will set up three pricing bands per tier: conservative, base, and aggressive. For now I will use our current average order value and margin as a starting point and flag any assumptions that need finance validation. We should also think about introductory discounts versus steady-state pricing so we do not overcomplicate the first launch.

Once the segment definitions are in A1, I will add a short narrative for the value proposition: what problem we solve, what benefit they get, and why a subscription is better than one-off purchases. I will keep it concise so we can later plug it into campaign messaging. I will also note any assumptions we might want to test quickly with a small customer survey before we finalize pricing.

Quick update on the sizing: based on last year data, the high-engagement existing customers are roughly 25 percent of our base, new digital-first customers around 15 percent, and lapsed customers about 20 percent. None of the groups looks too small for us to consider. The lapsed group might need different messaging, but from a volume standpoint it is viable.

Thanks for the numbers, that helps. Given that all three segments are meaningful, I suggest we proceed with them for the initial launch. For tiers, I propose we confirm the three-tier structure: Basic, Plus, Premium, with Plus as the expected main choice. We can still refine exact price points in T2, but we need to agree on the structure now so A1 and A6 stay consistent. Any strong objections to this direction?

No objections from my side. I have updated A1 with the three segments and the three tiers, including a short description for each. I left placeholders for final price ranges so they can be filled once T2 is further along. This should be enough for us to start thinking about the customer journey in the next thread as well.

I am aligned with the three segments and the three-tier structure. In the pricing model for T2, I will focus on making Plus clearly more attractive on value for money, with Basic as a low-commitment entry and Premium as a higher-benefit option. I will also outline a couple of discount rules and promo windows so finance can review them later.

Aligned as well. I will adjust the value proposition text in A1 to reflect Plus as the recommended option and make sure the messaging for Basic and Premium is still clear. Once we have initial price bands from T2, we can run a quick sense check against typical spend for each segment.

Summarizing where we landed so we can move forward: we will target three segments (high-engagement existing customers, new digital-first customers, and lapsed customers) and we will launch with three tiers (Basic, Plus, Premium), with Plus as the main option we expect most customers to choose. This gives us a clear structure for T1 and T2 and a solid base for A1 and A6. I will record this as our agreed direction so we can keep the rest of the plan consistent.

threads.thread_goal: Lock the go-to-market launch plan, channels and budget allocation.

messages.text: Sharing a first draft of the go-to-market launch plan and budget split so we can converge on channels and timing. I have outlined the main activities and owners in the Go-to-Market Launch Plan doc and mapped the spend by channel in the Launch Budget and Spend Tracker. The plan covers paid social, email, on-site placements, and a small test on retargeting. Please review with an eye on whether the channel mix supports our three segments and whether the timeline is realistic for asset production under T3 and T5.

Looking at A3, the structure makes sense. For our segments, email and on-site placements will be key for existing and lapsed customers, while paid social and retargeting will help with the newer digital-first group. One concern: the current timeline has only three days between finalizing messaging and starting asset production. For T5, that might be tight if we need multiple versions per tier. Could we shift the messaging approval earlier by two days to give creative a bit more room?

From a budget perspective, the split in A2 looks balanced, but I wonder if we should allocate slightly more to email and on-site, since those channels reach our existing base at lower cost. Maybe we can trim a bit from paid social and reassign to email testing and on-site personalization. I can run a quick scenario in A2 to see the impact on expected sign-ups and CAC, but I will need your view on minimum spend levels for the social test.

On the channel mix, I would like to make sure we have enough touchpoints for lapsed customers. In A3, I see email and retargeting, but maybe we should also include a small in-app or on-site banner for when they come back organically. That might not require much extra budget but could help remind them of the subscription when they browse.

I can help with the scenario in A2. I will duplicate the current budget tab and create an alternative where we reduce paid social by a small percentage and increase email and on-site accordingly. I will keep the total within the existing cap and highlight the differences so finance can review later under T7.

Good catch on the timing. We can move the messaging approval milestone earlier by two days without affecting the overall launch date. I will adjust A3 so that T5 has at least five days for asset production. That should reduce the risk of last-minute rush and quality issues.

Agree on adding an on-site banner for returning lapsed customers. I will update T3 details in A3 to include a dedicated placement on the homepage and account pages, with simple copy aligned to the value proposition we defined in A1. This should not require extra budget, just coordination with the web team.

Thanks for taking the scenario. Once you have the alternative split in A2, I will plug in rough conversion assumptions per channel so we can compare expected sign-ups. I will keep the assumptions simple and mark them clearly so we can refine later with actuals from A6 once the dashboard is live.

I have added the alternative budget split in A2. Paid social is reduced slightly, and email plus on-site now have a bit more room for testing. The total remains within the original cap. I flagged the new tab so it is easy to find.

With the on-site placements added in A3, the journey for lapsed customers looks more complete. We will have email, retargeting, and on-site prompts all pointing to the subscription landing page. For T5, we should ensure the creative brief includes specific variants for lapsed versus existing high-engagement customers so the messaging feels relevant.

I reviewed both budget options in A2 and the updated plan in A3. My proposal is to go with the alternative split that slightly favors email and on-site, while keeping a meaningful test on paid social and retargeting. The timeline with the earlier messaging approval also looks workable. Unless there are strong objections, I would like to confirm this channel mix and the launch timeline so we can move ahead with T3 and T5.

No objections from me. The adjusted mix still gives us enough reach on paid social while leaning into the more efficient channels. The updated timeline in A3 also gives us a better buffer for asset production and QA.

Aligned as well. I have added basic conversion assumptions to both budget tabs in A2, and the alternative split looks slightly better on expected CAC. We can refine once we have early data, but it is a solid starting point.
I am good with the proposed mix and the timeline. The plan in A3 now covers the key touchpoints for all three segments, and the production window for T5 feels more realistic.

Great, thanks for the input. To summarize: we will use the adjusted channel mix and budget split from the alternative tab in A2, with a stronger focus on email and on-site while keeping paid social and retargeting as meaningful tests. The launch timeline in A3 is confirmed with earlier messaging approval and a five-day asset production window under T5. I will record this as our agreed plan so we can brief creative and operations accordingly.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize customer journey, operational processes and readiness checklist.

messages.text: I have posted a draft of the end-to-end customer journey and the operational playbook for the subscription. The journey map in the Customer Journey and Experience Blueprint covers awareness through renewal and cancellation, and the Operational Playbook for Subscription Billing and Support outlines billing flows, renewals, and support scripts. I also started mapping these into the Pre-Launch Readiness and Quality Checklist so we can use it for T10. Please review with a focus on missing touchpoints, unclear ownership, or operational risks.

The journey in A4 looks comprehensive. One area I would like to clarify is the handoff between marketing and customer service when a subscriber has a billing issue during the first month. In A7, we have an escalation path, but it might help to add a specific step for proactive communication if a payment fails, so the customer does not just see a generic error.

From a control standpoint, I like that A5 already includes checks for billing accuracy and support readiness. I wonder if we should add a specific item to verify that renewal and cancellation flows are tested end-to-end before launch, not just sign-up. That would help reduce the risk of operational issues later.

In A7, I noticed we have scripts for common questions but not for customers who want to downgrade from Premium to Plus. Since we expect Plus to be the main tier, it might be useful to have a clear path for downgrades so agents know how to handle that without friction.

Good point on failed payments. We should define who owns the proactive communication and what the message looks like. I suggest customer service owns the outreach, with messaging aligned to the value proposition in A1. We can add a step in A4 for a triggered email and a corresponding script in A7.

Agree on testing renewals and cancellations. I will update A5 to include explicit checklist items for: 1) successful renewal, 2) voluntary cancellation, and 3) downgrade from Premium to Plus. I will also reflect these flows in T8 so the dry-run covers them before we sign off on T10.

I can draft the content for the failed payment email and the short explanation agents can use on calls or chat. I will base it on the value proposition in A1 and keep the tone reassuring, emphasizing that access will be restored quickly once the issue is resolved.

For the downgrade path, I will add a simple decision tree in A7 so agents know when to offer a downgrade versus when to suggest staying on Premium. I will keep it straightforward so it is easy to train.

With the new items in A5 and the expanded flows in A7, we should also think about how we log any issues during the dry-run. I suggest we add a column in the T10 checklist to capture owner and resolution date for each critical issue, so we can track them before launch.

Good idea. I will extend A5 with an issue log section tied to T10, including fields for owner, severity, and resolution date. That way, when we run the pre-launch review, we can document the go or no-go decision with clear evidence.

Looking at the updated A4, A7, and A5, the journey now covers awareness, sign-up, onboarding, billing, renewal, downgrade, and cancellation, with clear owners at each step. The checklist in A5 also includes the key quality checkpoints we discussed. Unless anyone sees a major gap, I suggest we confirm this as our baseline journey and readiness checklist for the launch.
I am comfortable with the journey and the checkpoints as they stand. The added steps for failed payments and downgrades close the main gaps I was worried about.
Aligned as well. The expanded checklist in A5 should help us catch operational issues early, especially around billing and renewals.
No further gaps from my side. The scripts and decision trees in A7 now cover the main customer scenarios we expect at launch.

Thanks everyone. To summarize: we are confirming the customer journey in A4, including the added steps for failed payments and downgrades, and we are approving the updated readiness checklist in A5 with explicit tests for sign-up, renewal, cancellation, and downgrade, plus the issue log for T10. The operational flows and scripts in A7 are our reference for billing and support. I will record this as our agreed baseline for launch readiness.

threads.thread_goal: Define KPI framework, dashboard spec and reporting cadence.

messages.text: I have drafted a first version of the KPI list and dashboard structure in the KPI Definitions and Dashboard Spec. It includes sign-ups by tier and segment, churn, ARPU, CAC by channel, and a simple payback view. The structure is also linked to the budget data in the Launch Budget and Spend Tracker. Please review and let me know if we are missing any critical metrics for the first 2–4 weeks post-launch, and how often you would like to see updates.

The KPI list in A6 covers the essentials. For the early phase, I would also like to track conversion from visit to subscription on the main landing page, broken down by channel if possible. That will help us see quickly which parts of the funnel need attention.

From a customer experience angle, it might be useful to include a simple metric for early engagement, such as percentage of new subscribers who use a key feature or benefit in the first week. Even if we approximate it at first, it will give us a sense of whether the value proposition is landing.

On reporting cadence, I suggest we have daily snapshots for the first week after launch, then move to a weekly summary. For the dashboard in T9, maybe we can have a top-level view for leadership and a more detailed tab for the team.

I like the structure. One thing I want to ensure is that definitions in A6 align with how finance will report revenue and costs. For CAC and ARPU, we should mirror their formulas as closely as possible. I can sync with finance to confirm, but we should at least document our assumptions clearly in T6.

I will add landing page conversion rate and, where data allows, a breakdown by channel to A6. For the first version of T9, I can set up a simple funnel view: visits, leads (if any), and subscriptions, with filters by channel.

For early engagement, we can start with a proxy such as percentage of subscribers who complete a key action in the first 7 days. I will add this to A6 and mark it as a phase-one metric, with the understanding that we might refine the definition later as we learn more.

Daily snapshots for the first week and weekly summaries after that sound reasonable. For T9, I can help design the layout so the top-level view shows sign-ups, churn, ARPU, and CAC, while the detailed tab includes breakdowns by tier, segment, and channel.

I will reach out to finance to confirm the formulas for CAC and ARPU and then update A6 accordingly. Until we get their confirmation, we can proceed with standard definitions but clearly label them as draft.

I can support by setting up the basic dashboard structure in our existing reporting tool for T9, using the spec in A6. Once the data connections are in place, we can iterate on the layout you proposed.

Sounds good. I will keep the current CAC and ARPU definitions in A6 as draft and add a note that they are pending finance confirmation. Once you have their feedback, I will update the formulas and make sure T9 reflects them.

With the funnel metrics added, we should be able to spot quickly if the issue is traffic quality, landing page, or pricing. For the weekly summaries, it might help to include a short narrative on what changed versus the previous week, not just the numbers.
I can take the lead on drafting the short narrative for the first few weekly summaries, using the dashboard in T9 as the source. That will help us build a consistent format for later.

Given the discussion, I propose we confirm the following: core KPIs are sign-ups by tier and segment, churn, ARPU, CAC by channel, landing page conversion, and early engagement, all defined in A6 and aligned with finance as soon as possible. Reporting cadence: daily snapshots for the first week post-launch, then weekly summaries with a short narrative. Does anyone see a need for additional core metrics at this stage?
No additional metrics from my side. The current list in A6 should give us a clear view of performance without overwhelming the team.
Aligned. The combination of funnel, financial, and engagement metrics should be enough to guide early optimizations.
I am aligned as well. I will finalize the definitions in A6 based on this list and make sure the dashboard spec in T9 matches.

Great, thanks everyone. To recap: we are confirming the core KPIs and their definitions in A6, including sign-ups by tier and segment, churn, ARPU, CAC by channel, landing page conversion, and early engagement. We are also agreeing on daily reporting for the first week after launch and weekly summaries with a short narrative afterward, using the dashboard built under T9. I will record this as our agreed framework for tracking the subscription launch.

threads.thread_goal: Coordinate launch week execution and capture early results and learnings.

messages.text: We are one day before launch. Let us use this thread to confirm go or no-go status, align on launch-day actions, and plan how we will capture early results. I have updated the Pre-Launch Readiness and Quality Checklist with the latest status. Please confirm your areas are green or flag any open issues that could affect T11. Also, think ahead to how we will log early learnings in the Post-Launch Review and Optimization Log and feed them into T12.

From the product side, sign-up, renewal, cancellation, and downgrade flows have passed the dry-run in T8 with no critical issues. A few minor UI text tweaks are still in progress but should be done today. I have marked all major items as green in A5.

On the data and KPI side, the dashboard in T9 is connected and pulling test data. I have validated key numbers against finance reports for a small sample, and they match within an acceptable range. Daily snapshot views for the first week are ready. I have also created a simple template in A8 to capture early performance and observations.

Customer journey touchpoints are in place: landing page, email flows, and on-site banners are live in staging and match the value proposition in A1 and the journey in A4. I ran through the main paths and did not see any blockers. I will do one more quick pass after the final UI text tweaks.

Support scripts and decision trees in A7 are finalized and shared with the customer service team. We ran a short role-play session to practice common scenarios, including failed payments and downgrades. I have marked the corresponding items as green in A5.

Thanks for the updates. Any remaining risks we should be aware of before we confirm go? For example, anything related to budget tracking in A2, or dependencies with other campaigns that might overlap with this launch?

On budget tracking, A2 is set up to capture actuals by channel starting tomorrow. The only open point is confirming how often finance wants updates, but that should not block launch. I will send them a note and adjust the tracker if needed.

No major risks from my side. The only thing to watch is response time on support during the first two days, in case we see more questions than expected. We have flagged this to the customer service manager, and they are planning extra coverage.

From a customer experience perspective, I would like us to keep an eye on early engagement metrics in the dashboard and capture any qualitative feedback from support in A8. That will help us prioritize quick wins for T12.

Given the status in A5 and the updates you all shared, I am comfortable proceeding with launch as planned. For tomorrow, let us align on a simple routine: daily async check-in in this channel with a snapshot from T11 and a short note on any issues or learnings. @59927, can you own posting the daily KPI snapshot from the dashboard?

Yes, I can own the daily KPI snapshot for the first week. I will pull the numbers from T9 each morning and post a brief summary with sign-ups, churn, and any notable changes in conversion or engagement. I will also log key points in A8 so we can use them in T12.

I will collect qualitative feedback from the support team during the first week and add a short section in A8 each day with common questions and pain points. That should help us spot patterns quickly.

I will monitor the product flows and landing page behavior on launch day and note any friction points. If we see anything critical, I will flag it here immediately and propose quick fixes where possible.
I can take the lead on drafting the initial post-launch review section in A8 at the end of the first week, summarizing what worked, what did not, and a first list of ideas for T12.

Perfect. To close this out: we are proceeding with launch tomorrow as planned, with all critical items in A5 marked green. T11 will cover execution and daily monitoring, with @59927 posting KPI snapshots and the rest of us feeding observations into A8. At the end of the first week, we will use A8 to define the optimization backlog for T12. Let us keep this thread for launch-week updates and use it as our main async standup.
